scope: the remaining VisA units of the MVTec/VisA generalization matrix (99 of 144 at the time of the switch)

concurrency.from: 1 (the runner's sequential loop, later 2 via the dispatcher)
concurrency.to: 3 concurrent units, throttled on free host RAM and free device memory

why.measured_cost: the score stage is 5.3x (candle, K=1) to 7.8x (pcb3, K=1) faster on the GPU, and the score stage is the K-proportional part, so the gain grows with K
why.measured_peaks: peak device memory was 2430 MiB for one small unit, 2600 MiB for one large unit, 2668 MiB for two and 3331 MiB for three, i.e. the per-process CUDA context dominates rather than the data
why.wall_clock: three K=8 large units took 159 s on 3-way GPU; the same three units sequentially on CPU are about 2500 s by extrapolation (pcb3 K=8 score is 758 s at the measured CPU rate)

parity_summary.unit: visa_s1_k1_candle, CPU vs GPU, same interpreter
parity_summary.verdict: numerically equivalent up to float32 accumulation order

consequence_for_the_artefact.statement: within the VisA batch the first 55 units were produced with device=cpu and torch 2.12.1, the remainder with device=cuda and torch 2.0.0; the 180 MVTec units are all cpu/torch 2.12.1
consequence_for_the_artefact.why_it_is_acceptable: pixel AP is a rank statistic over the patch maps; the measured device effect on it is 6.5e-07, four orders of magnitude below the effects reported in this study (about 5e-03) and well below the reported interval half-widths (about 4e-03)
consequence_for_the_artefact.residual_risk: the torch 2.12.1 vs 2.0.0 difference inside the CPU branch was not measured separately, so the mixed-batch statement rests on the device parity plus the fact that both builds compute the same float32 expression
consequence_for_the_artefact.mitigation: every unit records its own device-independent inputs (grid, labels, sample_ids) and the parity check is reproducible with scripts/limitation_closure_20260915/probe_device_parity.py

reversal: re-running the same unit ids with the recorded cpu interpreter overwrites the affected units; the runner skips nothing unless a unit is deleted, so a reversal must delete the DONE.json of the units to be recomputed
